newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends down before holiday weekend.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends down before holiday weekend.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled lower in an abbreviated session Thursday ahead of the three-day July 4th holiday weekend.
Market sources said the complex was under downward pressure early on profit-taking but prices rebounded when selling eased by midday.
"People were hesitant to be too short going into the weekend," a West Coast futures trader said.
August Palo Verde (PV) futures ended down 30 cents at $34.35 a megawatt hour (MWh), cutting a 85 cent loss.
September PV finished down 34 cents at $28.56 after reaching as low as $28.25. Most deferred months were inactive.
August California-Oregon Border (COB) settled down 28 cents at $23.02 after bouncing between $23.00 and $23.15.
September PV ended down 38 cents at $22.82. Most outer month contracts were quiet.
The power complex's early losses were reduced after PG&E Corp announced it will not restart its 1,070 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon 2 nuclear power unit today.
The company said it hopes to bring back the unit in Avila Beach, California, this weekend.
Market sources said the complex will likely head lower if Diablo Canyon 2 returns to service over the weekend.
The Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC), in its daily plant status report, indicated the unit may restart as early as Thursday after it was shut yesterday to repair a problem in the feedwater system.
Electricity futures this week were buoyed this week by unplanned outages of the Diablo Canyon unit and the San Onofre 2 nuclear unit in southern California.
The 1,070 MW San Onofre 2 was shut last Sunday to replace its charge line check valves, and the 1,080 MW San Onofre 3 has been offline since April 12 for refueling and maintenance.
San Onofre units 2 and 3 were expected to resume operation around July 15 and July 10, respectively.
In addition, capacity at the 1,221 MW Palo Verde 3 nuclear unit near Phoenix, Ariz., has been trimmed Wednesday by 15 percent for repair work expected to take 24 hours.
The 1,112 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state could restart this weekend if it were to receive approval from the NRC.

Almost 2,500 MW of coal-fired generation in the West are scheduled to resume operation by Monday. They include two 670 MW Centralia units in Washington, 330 MW Colstrip units in Montana, a 260 MW Hayden unit in Colorado and a 550 MW Laramie River unit in Wyoming.
In the cash market, firm, peak power prices at PV for Saturday and Monday fell to $26.50-28.00 from Wednesday's $29.00-30.00, while those at COB softened to $16.50-17.50 from $17.25-17.75 yesterday.
